claim: Checkpoint averaging within one training run gives no benefit once many seeds are already ensembled.
evidence: Measured: +0.87 sigma for a single model, falling to -0.01 sigma at 16 ensemble members (1 member +0.87, 3 members +0.28, 16 members -0.01).
scope: The k=16 seed-ensemble configuration that is currently submitted. Says nothing about single-model or small-ensemble regimes, where the effect was clearly real.
what_would_change_this: Evidence that checkpoints carry variance the seed ensemble does not already remove -- for example a training schedule with cyclic restarts, which produces genuinely different minima.

claim: Snapshot/top-N checkpoint ensembling dilutes rather than helps.
evidence: Rejected by its own guard: validation peaked at epoch 4 then declined, so the top-N checkpoints were one peak plus strictly worse neighbours from the same trajectory.
scope: ONE training configuration, whose epoch curve declines monotonically from an early peak. This is a property of that curve, not of the method.
what_would_change_this: Any configuration whose validation curve has several comparably-good epochs. Also note the guard compared against a checkpoint chosen on the SAME validation set, which biases against the method.

counterevidence.observation: Measured with held-out user splits instead of the biased guard, averaging the top-5 checkpoints beat argmax selection. The original rejection was an artefact of how it was compared.

claim: The recency decay of the pooled user history does not affect the score.
evidence: Paired 5-seed sweep against the default 3.0: tau=7 -0.01 sigma, tau=14 -0.07 sigma, tau=1 -0.00 sigma.
scope: The incumbent fm_numpy + bpr_pairwise + recency_weighted_pool configuration, tau in [1,14] days.
what_would_change_this: A different history mechanism, or tau far outside the 1-14 day range that was actually swept.
source: clean run 2 hypothesis, verified this session

claim: Within-user ranking metrics make any feature constant across a user's rows worthless, regardless of its global predictive power.
evidence: Structural: GAUC and nDCG@5 both rank WITHIN a user, so a user-constant feature shifts every one of that user's scores equally and changes no ordering.
scope: Both metrics in this competition. Holds by construction, not by measurement.
what_would_change_this: Nothing within this metric definition; it follows from the metric itself.
